en: In the wilderness of Sin the people grumble, wishing they had died by the pots of meat in Egypt.
The LORD says he will rain down bread from heaven, to test whether they follow his instructions.
That evening quail cover the camp; in the morning fine flakes lie on the ground.
"What is it?" they ask. Each gathers an omer per person; what is kept till morning breeds maggots.
On the sixth day they gather twice as much, for the seventh is a Sabbath, and none is found.
They call it manna: white like coriander seed, tasting like wafers made with honey.
A jar of manna is kept before the LORD. The Israelites eat manna for forty years.
zh: 在汛的曠野，百姓發怨言，說寧願死在埃及的肉鍋旁邊。
耶和華說要從天上降下糧食，考驗他們是否遵行他的律法。
當晚有鵪鶉遮滿營地；早晨地上有一層細小的薄片。
他們問：「這是甚麼？」每人收一俄梅珥；留到早晨的就生蟲。
第六天他們收雙倍，因為第七天是安息日，那天甚麼也找不到。
他們給它起名叫嗎哪，像白色的芫荽種子，味道像攙蜜的薄餅。
一罐嗎哪被存放在耶和華面前。以色列人吃嗎哪共四十年。

about.en: Jesus: "I am the bread of life"
about.zh: 耶穌說：「我就是生命的糧。」

about.en: Paul quotes 16:18 on gathering much and little
about.zh: 保羅引用16章18節論多收和少收

about.en: People do not live on bread alone
about.zh: 人活着不是單靠食物

about.en: The manna stops when Israel eats the produce of Canaan
about.zh: 以色列人吃了迦南的出產，嗎哪就停止了

en: Quail migrate across Sinai each spring and autumn; tired flocks landing near the coast have been caught in great numbers.
An omer, a tenth of an ephah (16:36), was about 2 litres; estimates of ancient measures vary.
The name manna comes from the people's question in Hebrew, man hu, "What is it?" (16:15).
zh: 鵪鶉每年春秋兩季飛越西奈；疲倦的鳥群在海邊降落時，常被人大量捕捉。
一俄梅珥是伊法的十分之一（16章36節），約兩公升；古代量器的估算各有不同。
「嗎哪」這名字來自百姓用希伯來文問的話 man hu，意思是「這是甚麼？」（16章15節）。

en: The community camps at Rephidim, and there is no water for the people to drink.
They quarrel with Moses and grumble: "Why did you bring us up out of Egypt, to kill us with thirst?"
Moses cries out to the LORD: "A little more and they will stone me!"
The LORD tells him to take some elders and the staff that struck the Nile, and go ahead of the people.
The LORD stands before him on the rock at Horeb; Moses strikes the rock, and water comes out.
He names the place Massah and Meribah, for they tested the LORD: "Is the LORD among us or not?"
zh: 以色列全會眾在利非訂安營，那裏沒有水給百姓喝。
他們與摩西爭吵，發怨言說：「你為甚麼把我們從埃及領出來，要叫我們渴死呢？」
摩西向耶和華呼求：「他們幾乎要拿石頭打死我了！」
耶和華吩咐他帶幾個長老，拿着擊打尼羅河的杖，走在百姓前面。
耶和華站在何烈的磐石那裏；摩西擊打磐石，水就流出來。
他給那地方起名叫瑪撒，又叫米利巴，因為他們試探耶和華說：「耶和華是不是在我們中間呢？」

about.en: Water from the rock again at Meribah; Moses strikes it twice
about.zh: 在米利巴磐石再次出水；摩西擊打兩次

about.en: A psalm warns: do not harden your hearts as at Meribah
about.zh: 詩篇警告：不要像在米利巴那樣硬着心

about.en: Paul: "the rock was Christ"
about.zh: 保羅說：「那磐石就是基督。」

about.en: Jesus: "If anyone is thirsty, let him come to me"
about.zh: 耶穌說：「人若渴了，可以到我這裏來喝。」

en: Rephidim's location is unknown; it is traditionally placed in Wadi Feiran in southern Sinai, on the way to Jebel Musa.
In Hebrew Massah means "testing" and Meribah means "quarreling".
zh: 利非訂的位置不詳；傳統上認為在西奈半島南部的費蘭谷，位於往穆薩山的路上。
希伯來文「瑪撒」的意思是「試探」，「米利巴」的意思是「爭吵」。

en: In the third month after leaving Egypt, Israel camps in front of the mountain in the wilderness of Sinai.
God says that if they keep his covenant, they will be his treasured possession, a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.
The people answer, "We will do everything the LORD has said," and prepare themselves for the third day.
On the third day come thunder, lightning, a thick cloud and a loud ram's horn; the mountain smokes and shakes.
God speaks: no other gods, no idols, no misuse of his name; keep the Sabbath; honor father and mother.
Do not murder, commit adultery, steal, give false testimony or covet your neighbor's things.
Trembling, the people stand at a distance and ask Moses to speak to them instead of God.
zh: 出埃及後第三個月，以色列人來到西奈的曠野，在山前安營。
神說，他們若遵守他的約，就要作他的珍寶，作祭司的國度、聖潔的國民。
百姓回答說：「凡耶和華所說的，我們都要遵行。」並且潔淨自己，準備第三天。
第三天有雷轟、閃電、密雲和很響的角聲；全山冒煙，劇烈震動。
神說：不可有別的神，不可造偶像，不可妄稱他的名；要守安息日，要孝敬父母。
不可殺人，不可姦淫，不可偷盜，不可作假見證，不可貪戀鄰舍的東西。
百姓戰兢，遠遠站着，求摩西代替神對他們說話。

about.en: Moses repeats the Ten Commandments
about.zh: 摩西重述十誡

about.en: Jesus names the greatest commandments
about.zh: 耶穌指出最大的誡命

about.en: Mount Sinai and Mount Zion compared
about.zh: 西奈山與錫安山的對比

en: Treaties of the 14th and 13th centuries BC, such as the Hittite ones, open with the great king's name and past deeds before his demands, as 20:2 does.
Exodus 34:28 calls them the "ten words"; Jews and Christians divide and number the ten in different ways.
Mount Sinai is traditionally Jebel Musa (about 2,285 m) in southern Sinai; others propose sites in northern Sinai or northwest Arabia.
zh: 公元前十四、十三世紀的條約（例如赫人的條約），先寫大君王的名號和他過去的作為，然後才列出要求，與20章2節的寫法相似。
出埃及記34章28節稱這些為「十句話」；猶太人和基督徒對十誡的劃分和編號各有不同。
傳統認為西奈山就是西奈半島南部的穆薩山（約2285米）；也有人認為在西奈北部或阿拉伯半島西北部。

en: Moses is long on the mountain, so the people ask Aaron, "Make us gods who will go ahead of us."
Aaron makes a calf of cast metal from their gold earrings, and they say, "These are your gods, Israel."
The LORD tells Moses to go down and says he will destroy the people. Moses pleads, and the LORD relents.
Seeing the calf and the dancing, Moses throws down the tablets and breaks them.
He burns the calf, grinds it to powder, scatters it on water and makes the Israelites drink it.
The Levites rally to Moses, and about three thousand people die that day.
Moses asks God to forgive them, or else to wipe him out of the book he has written.
zh: 摩西遲遲沒有下山，百姓就對亞倫說：「給我們造神像，在我們前面引路。」
亞倫用他們的金耳環鑄了一頭牛犢；他們說：「以色列啊，這就是你的神。」
耶和華叫摩西下山，說要滅絕百姓。摩西懇求，耶和華就改變心意。
摩西看見牛犢和跳舞的人，就把兩塊版扔下摔碎了。
他把牛犢燒了，磨成粉末，撒在水面上，叫以色列人喝。
利未人聚集到摩西那裏；那一天約有三千人倒下。
摩西求神赦免他們，不然就把他從神所寫的冊子上塗抹掉。

about.en: Stephen tells how Israel made the calf
about.zh: 司提反講述以色列人造牛犢

about.en: Paul quotes 32:6: "The people sat down to eat and drink"
about.zh: 保羅引用32章6節：「百姓坐下吃喝」

about.en: Moses cuts new tablets, and the LORD proclaims his name
about.zh: 摩西鑿出新的石版，耶和華宣告他的名

about.en: Jeroboam makes two gold calves: "Here are your gods"
about.zh: 耶羅波安造了兩頭金牛犢

en: Bulls were common religious symbols in Egypt (the Apis bull) and in Canaan; a small bronze and silver calf from about 1550 BC was found at Ashkelon in 1990.
Ancient idols were carved in wood and overlaid with gold, or cast in metal (compare Isaiah 40:19); 32:4 says Aaron cast the calf and shaped it with a tool.
zh: 公牛在埃及（阿匹斯神牛）和迦南都是常見的宗教象徵；1990年在亞實基倫出土了一頭約公元前1550年的銅鍍銀小牛像。
古代的偶像有用木頭雕刻再包金的，也有用金屬鑄造的（參看以賽亞書40章19節）；32章4節說亞倫鑄成牛犢，並用工具塑造。

en: The LORD asks for a contribution from all whose hearts move them: gold, silver, bronze, yarn, linen, wood.
"Have them make a sanctuary for me, so that I may live among them," exactly like the pattern shown.
An ark of acacia wood overlaid with gold, with a gold cover and two cherubim, will hold the testimony.
There are also a table, a gold lampstand, curtains and frames, a bronze altar and a courtyard.
On the first day of the first month in the second year, Moses sets up the tabernacle.
The cloud covers the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD fills the tabernacle.
When the cloud lifts, the Israelites set out; if it does not lift, they stay.
zh: 耶和華吩咐凡甘心樂意的人獻上禮物：金、銀、銅、各色紗線、細麻和木頭。
「他們要為我造聖所，好讓我住在他們中間。」一切都要照着所指示的式樣。
要用皂莢木造櫃，包上精金，上面有金的施恩座和兩個基路伯，櫃裏放法版。
還要造桌子、金燈臺、幔子和豎板、銅祭壇和院子。
第二年正月初一，摩西把帳幕立起來。
雲彩遮蓋會幕，耶和華的榮耀充滿了帳幕。
雲彩升起，以色列人就起行；雲彩不升起，他們就不起行。

about.en: The Word became flesh and lived among us
about.zh: 道成了肉身，住在我們中間

about.en: The tabernacle as a copy and shadow of what is in heaven
about.zh: 帳幕是天上事物的副本和影子

about.en: "God's dwelling is with humankind"
about.zh: 「神的居所在人間」

en: A cubit was the length from elbow to fingertip, about 45 cm, so the ark was about 1.1 m long and 0.7 m wide and high.
The courtyard was 100 by 50 cubits (27:18), about 45 by 23 metres.
Portable shrines of wooden frames overlaid with gold are known from Egypt, such as those in Tutankhamun's tomb (about 1325 BC).
zh: 一肘是從手肘到指尖的長度，約45厘米；所以約櫃約長1.1米，寬和高各約0.7米。
院子長一百肘，寬五十肘（27章18節），約45米長、23米寬。
埃及也有用木架包金、可以拆卸搬運的神龕，例如圖坦卡門墓（約公元前1325年）中的神龕。

en: At the LORD's command Moses sends twelve men, one from each tribe, to explore Canaan.
In the Valley of Eshcol they cut a single cluster of grapes, which two men carry on a pole.
After forty days they report: the land flows with milk and honey, but its people are strong and its towns fortified.
Caleb says, "Let us go up at once"; the others say, "We seemed like grasshoppers."
The people weep and want a leader to take them back to Egypt; Joshua and Caleb urge them not to rebel.
Moses pleads, and the LORD forgives; but none of that generation will see the land, except Caleb and Joshua.
Against Moses' word they go up anyway and are beaten back by the Amalekites and Canaanites.
zh: 摩西照耶和華的吩咐，從每個支派派一人，共十二人，去窺探迦南地。
他們在以實各谷砍下一串葡萄，要兩個人用槓抬着。
四十天後他們回來報告：那地確實流奶與蜜，但居民強壯，城邑堅固。
迦勒說：「我們立刻上去吧！」其他人卻說：「我們看自己就像蚱蜢一樣。」
百姓哭號，要另立首領回埃及去；約書亞和迦勒勸他們不要背叛耶和華。
摩西懇求，耶和華就赦免了；但那一代人除了迦勒和約書亞，都不得看見那地。
他們不聽摩西的話，硬要上去，結果被亞瑪力人和迦南人擊退。

about.en: Forty-five years later, Caleb receives Hebron
about.zh: 四十五年後，迦勒得了希伯崙為業

about.en: Only Caleb and Joshua followed the LORD wholeheartedly
about.zh: 只有迦勒和約書亞專心跟從耶和華

about.en: They could not enter because of unbelief
about.zh: 他們因為不信，不能進入

en: Kadesh (Kadesh-barnea) is usually identified with the springs of Ein el-Qudeirat in northeast Sinai, near today's Egypt–Israel border.
Hebron lies about 30 km south of Jerusalem; vineyards still grow around it, and the Valley of Eshcol ("cluster") is traditionally placed nearby.
Numbers 13:22 says Hebron was built seven years before Zoan (Tanis), a city in the northeast Nile Delta.
zh: 加低斯（加低斯‧巴尼亞）一般認為是西奈東北部的古德拉泉，靠近今天埃及和以色列的邊界。
希伯崙在耶路撒冷以南約30公里，周圍至今仍有葡萄園；以實各谷（意思是「一串」）傳統上認為就在附近。
民數記13章22節說，希伯崙比鎖安（坦尼斯）早七年建造；鎖安是尼羅河三角洲東北部的城。

en: Korah the Levite, with Dathan, Abiram and On and 250 leaders, rises up against Moses and Aaron.
They say, "The whole community is holy. Why do you exalt yourselves?"
Moses tells them to bring firepans with incense, so that the LORD will show whom he chooses.
He asks the Levites: is it not enough to serve the LORD, that you seek the priesthood as well?
Dathan and Abiram refuse to come, saying Moses brought them from a land of milk and honey to die.
The ground splits open and swallows them and their households; they go down alive into Sheol.
Fire from the LORD consumes the 250 men who were offering the incense.
zh: 利未人可拉，聯同大坍、亞比蘭、安和二百五十個領袖，起來反抗摩西和亞倫。
他們說：「全會眾個個都是聖潔的，你們為甚麼抬高自己？」
摩西叫他們拿火鼎盛香，看耶和華揀選誰。
他問利未人：神使你們親近他事奉他，還不夠嗎？你們還要求祭司的職分嗎？
大坍和亞比蘭不肯來，說摩西把他們從流奶與蜜之地領出來，要害死他們。
地裂開了，把他們和他們的家都吞下去；他們活活地墜入陰間。
有火從耶和華那裏出來，燒滅了那二百五十個獻香的人。

about.en: Aaron's staff sprouts, showing the LORD has chosen him
about.zh: 亞倫的杖發芽，顯明耶和華揀選他

about.en: "But the sons of Korah did not die"
about.zh: 「但可拉的兒子們沒有死」

about.en: A psalm headed "of the sons of Korah"
about.zh: 一篇題為「可拉後裔」的詩

about.en: Jude warns of those who perish "in Korah's rebellion"
about.zh: 猶大書警告那些「在可拉的叛亂中滅亡」的人

en: Eleven psalms (42, 44–49, 84–85, 87–88) carry the title "of the sons of Korah"; the Korahites became Levite singers (2 Chronicles 20:19).
A firepan carried live coals; incense laid on the coals gave off fragrant smoke.
This site follows the Hebrew numbering: Numbers 17:1–15 here is 16:36–50 in most English Bibles, and 17:16–28 is 17:1–13.
zh: 有十一篇詩篇（42，44至49，84至85，87至88篇）題為「可拉後裔的詩」；可拉的子孫後來成了利未族的歌唱者（歷代志下20章19節）。
火鼎是用來盛炭火的器具；把香放在炭火上，就冒出香煙。
本站依照希伯來文的節數：這裏的民數記17章1至15節，在多數英文聖經是16章36至50節；17章16至28節則是17章1至13節。

title.en: Wandering in the wilderness; the bronze serpent

en: The LORD says all of the grumbling community aged twenty and older will die in the wilderness.
Only Caleb and Joshua will enter; the children will be shepherds in the wilderness for forty years.
The forty days of exploring become forty years: a year for each day.
Years later, going around Edom, the people grow impatient and speak against God and Moses.
The LORD sends fiery snakes; many die, and the people confess their sin and ask Moses to pray.
Moses makes a bronze snake and puts it on a pole; anyone bitten who looks at it lives.
zh: 耶和華說，那些發怨言的會眾，凡二十歲以上的，都要倒斃在曠野。
只有迦勒和約書亞能進去；他們的兒女要在曠野放牧四十年。
窺探那地的四十天，一天算一年，成了四十年。
多年後，他們繞過以東地，百姓在路上不耐煩，就埋怨神和摩西。
耶和華使火蛇進入百姓中，死了許多人；百姓認罪，求摩西禱告。
摩西造了一條銅蛇，掛在杆子上；被蛇咬的人一望銅蛇，就活下來。

about.en: Jesus: as Moses lifted up the snake, so the Son of Man
about.zh: 耶穌說：摩西怎樣舉蛇，人子也必照樣被舉起

about.en: Hezekiah breaks up the bronze snake, called Nehushtan
about.zh: 希西家打碎那叫尼忽士但的銅蛇

about.en: Thirty-eight years until that generation had died out
about.zh: 三十八年後，那一代人都死盡了

about.en: Paul: those destroyed by the snakes are a warning
about.zh: 保羅說：被蛇所滅的事是給我們的警戒

en: Edom lay south and southeast of the Dead Sea, in today's southern Jordan.
Venomous snakes, such as the saw-scaled viper and the horned viper, live in Sinai and the Arabah valley.
A copper snake about 13 cm long was found in a shrine at Timna, a copper-mining site in the Arabah, from about the 12th century BC.
zh: 以東位於死海的南面和東南面，在今天約旦的南部。
西奈和亞拉巴谷有毒蛇出沒，例如鋸鱗蝰和角蝰。
在亞拉巴谷的銅礦遺址亭納，一座約公元前十二世紀的神廟中，出土了一條長約13厘米的銅蛇。

en: Moab is terrified of Israel, camped on its plains, so King Balak sends for Balaam son of Beor to curse them.
God tells Balaam, "You must not curse the people, for they are blessed."
Balak sends more officials. God lets Balaam go, but he must do only what God tells him.
On the road his donkey sees the angel of the LORD and turns aside three times; the LORD opens the donkey's mouth.
The LORD opens Balaam's eyes to see the angel, who tells him to say only what he is told.
Three times Balak builds altars for a curse, and three times Balaam blesses Israel instead.
Balaam says, "A star will march out of Jacob; a scepter will rise out of Israel." Then each goes home.
zh: 以色列人在摩押平原安營，摩押人非常害怕；摩押王巴勒派人去請比珥的兒子巴蘭來咒詛他們。
神對巴蘭說：「你不可咒詛那民，因為他們是蒙福的。」
巴勒又派更多的使臣去。神讓巴蘭去，但他只可照神的吩咐行。
在路上，母驢看見耶和華的使者，三次轉開；耶和華就開了母驢的口。
耶和華開了巴蘭的眼睛，他就看見那使者；使者吩咐他只說所吩咐的話。
巴勒三次築壇要咒詛以色列，巴蘭卻三次為以色列祝福。
巴蘭說：「必有一顆星從雅各而出，必有一根權杖從以色列興起。」然後各自回去。

about.en: Peter: Balaam rebuked by a speaking donkey
about.zh: 彼得說：巴蘭被會說話的驢責備

about.en: Balaam son of Beor is killed with the kings of Midian
about.zh: 比珥的兒子巴蘭和米甸諸王一同被殺

about.en: "The teaching of Balaam", who taught Balak
about.zh: 教導巴勒的「巴蘭的教訓」

about.en: Micah: remember what Balak planned and Balaam answered
about.zh: 彌迦說：要記得巴勒的計謀和巴蘭的回答

en: A plaster inscription found at Deir Alla in Jordan, from about 800 BC, tells of "Balaam son of Beor", a seer of the gods.
The plains of Moab lie northeast of the Dead Sea, across the Jordan from Jericho; Moab itself was east of the Dead Sea, in today's central Jordan.
Pethor (22:5) is usually identified with Pitru on the Euphrates, south of Carchemish, known from Assyrian records.
zh: 在約旦代爾阿拉出土的一段約公元前800年的灰泥銘文，記載了「比珥的兒子巴蘭」，稱他為眾神的先見。
摩押平原在死海東北，與耶利哥隔着約旦河相望；摩押本土在死海以東，即今天約旦的中部。
毗奪（22章5節）通常認為就是亞述文獻中的皮特魯，在伯拉河邊、迦基米施以南。

title.zh: 摩西的臨別之言；約書亞接續帶領

en: Moses, 120 years old, tells Israel he will not cross the Jordan; the LORD will go ahead of them, with Joshua.
Before all Israel he tells Joshua, "Be strong and courageous," for the LORD will not abandon him.
Moses writes the law in a book, and the LORD commissions Joshua at the tent of meeting.
From Mount Nebo the LORD shows Moses the land he swore to give to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
Moses dies in Moab, and no one knows where his grave is. Israel mourns for him thirty days.
Joshua is filled with the spirit of wisdom, for Moses had laid his hands on him.
The LORD tells Joshua to cross the Jordan and keep the law: "As I was with Moses, so I will be with you."
zh: 摩西一百二十歲了，他告訴以色列人：他不能過約旦河，耶和華要親自在前面行，約書亞要帶領他們。
他在以色列眾人眼前對約書亞說：「你要剛強，要壯膽。」因為耶和華必不丟棄他。
摩西把律法寫在書上；耶和華在會幕那裏任命約書亞。
耶和華在尼波山上把他向亞伯拉罕、以撒和雅各起誓應許的地指給摩西看。
摩西死在摩押地，沒有人知道他的墳墓在哪裏。以色列人為他哀哭了三十天。
約書亞充滿了智慧的靈，因為摩西曾按手在他頭上。
耶和華吩咐約書亞過約旦河，遵守律法，又說：「我怎樣與摩西同在，也必照樣與你同在。」

about.en: Moses lays his hands on Joshua and commissions him
about.zh: 摩西按手在約書亞頭上，任命他

about.en: Peter quotes Moses: God will raise up a prophet like me
about.zh: 彼得引用摩西的話：神要興起一位像我的先知

about.en: "I will never fail you or abandon you" (Deuteronomy 31:6)
about.zh: 「我總不撇下你，也不丟棄你」（申31章6節）

about.en: Moses appears with Elijah, talking with Jesus
about.zh: 摩西和以利亞顯現，與耶穌說話

en: Mount Nebo, about 800 m high, is in Jordan, northeast of the Dead Sea; on clear days Jericho and the hills of Jerusalem can be seen from it.
A church built on Nebo by the 4th century AD marks the traditional place of Moses' death; his grave is unknown (34:6).
The name Deuteronomy means "second law" in Greek, from the Greek translation of 17:18.
zh: 尼波山約高800米，在今天約旦境內、死海東北；天晴時可以從山上望見耶利哥和耶路撒冷的山嶺。
尼波山上有一座最晚建於公元四世紀的教堂，是傳統上紀念摩西去世的地方；他的墳墓卻無人知道（34章6節）。
「申命記」的英文名 Deuteronomy 來自希臘文，意思是「第二律法」，出自希臘文譯本對17章18節的翻譯。

en: Joshua secretly sends two spies from Shittim; they stay in Jericho at the house of a prostitute named Rahab.
The king of Jericho orders her to bring them out, but she hides them under stalks of flax on her roof.
She sends the pursuers off on the road to the fords of the Jordan.
She tells the spies: we heard how the LORD dried up the Red Sea; your God is God in heaven and on earth.
She asks them to swear to spare her family, and they promise, "Our lives for yours."
She lets them down by a rope from her window in the town wall, and ties a scarlet cord in the window.
After three days in the hills they tell Joshua, "The LORD has given the whole land into our hands."
zh: 約書亞從什亭暗中派兩個探子去；他們在耶利哥一個名叫喇合的妓女家裏過夜。
耶利哥王叫她把那兩人交出來，她卻把他們藏在房頂的麻稈下。
她打發追趕的人往約旦河渡口的路上去。
她對探子說：我們聽見耶和華怎樣使紅海的水乾了；耶和華你們的神是上天下地的神。
她求他們起誓保全她全家，他們答應說：「我們願意替你們死！」
她用繩子把他們從城牆上的窗戶吊下去，又把朱紅色的繩子繫在窗上。
他們在山上躲了三天，回去對約書亞說：「耶和華已經把那全地交在我們手中了。」

about.en: Rahab and her family are spared at Jericho
about.zh: 喇合和她全家在耶利哥得以存活

about.en: Rahab in the family line of Jesus
about.zh: 喇合列在耶穌的家譜中

about.en: By faith Rahab did not perish
about.zh: 喇合因着信沒有滅亡

about.en: James: Rahab welcomed the messengers
about.zh: 雅各書說：喇合接待了使者

en: Jericho, by a strong spring north of the Dead Sea, is one of the oldest known towns in the world; its ancient mound is Tell es-Sultan.
Flax was grown for linen; after harvest its stalks were soaked and then dried, often spread on flat roofs.
Shittim ("acacias") was Israel's last camp on the plains of Moab, east of the Jordan.
zh: 耶利哥位於死海以北的一道大泉旁，是世上已知最古老的城鎮之一；古城遺址是蘇丹丘。
亞麻是用來織細麻布的；收割後，麻稈先浸水，再曬乾，常常鋪在平的房頂上。
什亭（意思是「皂莢樹」）是以色列人在約旦河東、摩押平原的最後一個營地。

title.en: Israel enters the promised land: the Jordan and Jericho
title.zh: 以色列進入應許之地：過約旦河，攻取耶利哥

en: The priests carry the ark into the Jordan, flooding at harvest time, and the water stops far upstream at Adam.
All Israel crosses on dry ground while the priests stand in the middle of the river.
Twelve stones from the riverbed are set up at Gilgal as a sign for their children.
At Gilgal they keep the Passover; after they eat the produce of the land, the manna stops.
Near Jericho the commander of the LORD's army appears to Joshua.
For six days the soldiers and seven priests with rams' horns march once around the town with the ark.
On the seventh day they march around seven times; the people shout, and the wall collapses.
zh: 祭司抬着約櫃進入收割時漲滿兩岸的約旦河，上游的水就在遠處的亞當城停住。
祭司站在河中間的乾地上，以色列眾人都踏着乾地過去。
他們從河中取了十二塊石頭，立在吉甲，作為給子孫的記號。
他們在吉甲守逾越節；吃了那地的出產以後，嗎哪就停止了。
在耶利哥附近，耶和華軍隊的元帥向約書亞顯現。
一連六天，軍兵和七個拿着羊角號的祭司抬着約櫃，每天繞城一次。
第七天，他們繞城七次；百姓大聲吶喊，城牆就倒塌了。

about.en: A psalm: the sea fled and the Jordan turned back
about.zh: 詩篇：海看見就逃跑，約旦河也倒流

about.en: By faith the walls of Jericho fell
about.zh: 耶利哥的城牆因着信倒塌

about.en: Hiel rebuilds Jericho, as Joshua's curse had said
about.zh: 希伊勒重建耶利哥，應驗了約書亞的話

en: Adam is usually identified with Tell ed-Damiyeh, about 30 km up the Jordan; landslides there blocked the river for hours in AD 1267 and 1927.
Archaeologists differ on Jericho in Joshua's day: Kathleen Kenyon dated the fall of its walled city to about 1550 BC; others argue for about 1400 BC.
Gilgal was east of Jericho (4:19); its exact site has not been identified.
zh: 亞當城一般認為是約旦河上游約30公里的達米耶丘；公元1267年和1927年，那裏的山崩曾把河水截斷了幾個小時。
考古學家對約書亞時代的耶利哥意見不一：肯揚把這座有城牆的城被毀定在約公元前1550年，也有人主張約公元前1400年。
吉甲在耶利哥以東（4章19節），確實位置至今未能確定。
